note: Independent evidence next to each answer. The operator's log is one source, not ground truth; where sources disagree, both are shown.

track_record.question: Did this turbine stop for 60 minutes or more at wind of 4 m/s or more?
track_record.answered_by: time-series language model (OpenTSLM + fusion adapter, 3 seeds)
track_record.test: Trained on Senvion; alarm level set on Senvion only; Hill of Towie (Siemens, never seen) 2016-2021, scored once
track_record.result: 91.6% of 2,556 stops caught, 8 false alarms in 37,899 turbine-days (gradient boosting: 73.2%, 5)
track_record.limits: Gradient boosting ranks stop days slightly better (average precision 0.996 vs 0.989). Stops under 60 minutes are not in the test.

track_record.question: Was this turbine told to cut its output?
track_record.test: Hill of Towie 2025-26, 768 turbine-days on 37 grid-dispatch dates
track_record.limits: On later Senvion logged days 42.5% caught; most show no drop in power.

track_record.question: Is this turbine running below what its wind should give?
track_record.answered_by: gradient-boosting tree, frozen (our language model failed its validation bar)
track_record.test: Real events on Kelmarsh and Penmanshiel never used in training (a logged power cap, wind-sensor faults); in-fleet: these turbines' other windows were in training; alarm level set on Fuhrländer
track_record.result: 16 of 19 capped 30-day windows caught; 0 of 56 sensor-fault windows called a loss (52 named a sensor fault)
track_record.limits: No ground truth for real running losses beyond these events. On a new farm (EDP) the Fuhrländer threshold, carried over unchanged, flags 18% of ordinary windows: it does not transfer (planned fix: calibrate on the new farm's first 90 days). Our rule-based detector failed its pre-registered Hill of Towie test: 7.7-13.7% of ordinary 30-day windows flagged.

track_record.question: How much energy did this stop cost?
track_record.answered_by: code (energy below the expected power curve)
track_record.test: Against the operator's own lost-energy figure

track_record.question: Was it the weather or the turbine side?
track_record.test: Fresh 2023-24 test, bar set in advance (macro F1 0.8+, energy share within 5 points, both farms)
track_record.result: 312 of 313 comment-labelled stops right; energy split within 3.4 points: HOLDS
track_record.limits: Within the fleet it trained on. At home the language model fell short of the tree (2016-18 test, mostly where pitch was not recorded).

track_record.question: Weather or turbine side, on a maker it never saw?
track_record.answered_by: time-series language model (trained on Senvion stops, frozen)
track_record.test: Hill of Towie (Siemens) 2016-2024, 1,741 stops, scored once; nothing trained or tuned there; bar set in advance
track_record.result: F1 0.838 against the tree's 0.766 (+0.072, 95% interval +0.032 to +0.116): PASS; 748 of 876 weather stops found against 635
track_record.limits: One Siemens farm; labels from controller stop timers whose meaning is not officially documented; no maintenance class.

track_record.question: Did the fix work?
track_record.test: AeroUp blades on Hill of Towie T13, bar set in advance
track_record.result: Reference B +6.9% [-4.1, +9.6], reference A +8.0% [+6.7, +13.3] over 53 days: not yet confirmed
track_record.limits: The interval for B still includes 0; more months will narrow it.

loop_rule: An engineer's verdict is stored as 'pending check'. It becomes a training label only when independent evidence (the second wind sensor, grid-dispatch records, the grid meter, the operator's own energy figure) agrees with it. A retrained model replaces the current one only if it beats it on the fixed public tests.

stops_kelmarsh.rule_energy_close: within 20% or 0.5 MWh of the operator's figure

log_wrong_case.title: The log said icing. The evidence says a broken wind sensor.
log_wrong_case.evidence: On 31 of the 32 stops the turbine's two anemometers disagreed far more than usual (split -0.19 to -0.08, against about -0.02 on healthy turbines); on the other 1, both read 37% or more above the neighbouring turbines. Turbines with agreeing anemometers in the same weather did not ice.
log_wrong_case.why_it_matters: A model trained on the log would learn that this weather causes icing, and would call sensor faults weather.
